title: a brand's success
meaning_vi: sự thành công của một thương hiệu

examples.en: The key factors behind a brand's success are: product, price, place, and promotion.

title: associating a product with a certain lifestyle
term: associating a product with a certain lifestyle
pronunciation: /əˌsəʊʃiˈeɪtɪŋ ə ˈprɒdʌkt wɪð ə ˈsɜːtn ˈlaɪfstaɪl/
meaning_vi: (verb phrase (gerund)). gắn một sản phẩm với một lối sống nhất định

examples.en: Sports brands frequently succeed by associating a product with a certain lifestyle that appeals to young buyers.

title: be attributed to
meaning_vi: được cho là do, bắt nguồn từ

examples.en: The brand's rapid growth can be attributed to its clever use of celebrity endorsements.

title: boost sales
meaning_vi: thúc đẩy doanh số

examples.en: Many companies rely on catchy slogans to boost sales during the holiday season, even when the products themselves have changed little.

title: brand differentiation
meaning_vi: sự khác biệt hóa thương hiệu

examples.en: Distinctive packaging is one of the simplest ways to achieve brand differentiation on crowded supermarket shelves.

title: build brand loyalty
meaning_vi: xây dựng lòng trung thành với thương hiệu

examples.en: Companies invest heavily in emotional storytelling to build brand loyalty that outlasts any single advertising campaign.

title: capturing consumer attention
meaning_vi: thu hút sự chú ý của người tiêu dùng

examples.en: Bright colours and catchy jingles remain effective tools for capturing consumer attention in a crowded market.

title: carefully crafted campaigns
meaning_vi: những chiến dịch được xây dựng tỉ mỉ, công phu

meaning_vi: tạo sự khác biệt so với các sản phẩm khác

examples.en: Distinctive packaging and slogans help brands create differentiation from other products on crowded shelves.

title: delineate product features
meaning_vi: mô tả rõ ràng các tính năng sản phẩm

examples.en: A well-designed advertisement should delineate product features clearly rather than relying on vague slogans.

title: depict a luxurious way of living
term: depict a luxurious way of living
meaning_vi: khắc họa một lối sống xa hoa

examples.en: Many perfume advertisements depict a luxurious way of living to make their products seem more desirable.

title: disseminating
meaning_vi: phổ biến, truyền bá

examples.en: Public health campaigns rely on advertising for disseminating important safety information quickly.

title: dissemination of information
meaning_vi: sự phổ biến thông tin

examples.en: Advertising plays a vital role in the dissemination of information about new products and services.

title: eco-friendly smartphone
meaning_vi: điện thoại thông minh thân thiện với môi trường

examples.en: The firm's latest eco-friendly smartphone is made from recycled materials and marketed as a sustainable choice.

title: exemplifies
meaning_vi: minh họa, là ví dụ điển hình cho

examples.en: The rise of viral marketing campaigns exemplifies how advertising has adapted to social media culture.

title: flash sales
meaning_vi: đợt giảm giá chớp nhoáng

examples.en: Online retailers frequently run flash sales to create a sense of urgency among shoppers.

title: give new products recognition
meaning_vi: giúp sản phẩm mới được nhận biết

examples.en: A well-planned launch campaign can give new products recognition before they even reach store shelves.

title: heavy promotional efforts
meaning_vi: nỗ lực quảng bá mạnh mẽ

examples.en: Despite heavy promotional efforts, the poorly designed product ultimately failed in the market.

title: increase its sales
meaning_vi: tăng doanh số bán hàng

examples.en: The startup hoped a viral video would increase its sales without any paid promotion.

title: increase products' attractiveness to consumers
meaning_vi: làm tăng sức hấp dẫn của sản phẩm đối với người tiêu dùng

examples.en: Bright packaging alone can increase products' attractiveness to consumers even before they read the label.

title: innovative
meaning_vi: sáng tạo, đổi mới

examples.en: Tech companies often use advertising to highlight the innovative features of their latest devices.

title: limited-time deals and flash sales
meaning_vi: ưu đãi có thời hạn và đợt giảm giá chớp nhoáng

examples.en: Online retailers frequently use limited-time deals and flash sales to pressure shoppers into impulsive purchases.

title: limited-time offer
meaning_vi: ưu đãi có thời hạn giới hạn

examples.en: The retailer advertised a limited-time offer to pressure shoppers into buying before the discount expired.

title: market identity
meaning_vi: bản sắc thị trường

examples.en: A consistent logo and tone of voice help a company build a strong market identity over time.

title: marketing gimmicks
meaning_vi: chiêu trò tiếp thị

examples.en: Savvy shoppers have learned to see through common marketing gimmicks such as fake countdown timers.

title: mass advertising campaigns
meaning_vi: các chiến dịch quảng cáo đại chúng

examples.en: Multinational corporations rely on mass advertising campaigns to build brand recognition worldwide.

title: Memorable slogans
meaning_vi: khẩu hiệu dễ nhớ

examples.en: Memorable slogans can stay in the public consciousness for decades, long after a campaign has ended.

title: niche markets
meaning_vi: thị trường ngách

examples.en: Small manufacturers often thrive by targeting niche markets that larger companies overlook.

title: offerings
meaning_vi: sản phẩm/dịch vụ cung cấp

examples.en: The company used a nationwide campaign to showcase its new product offerings to consumers.

title: persuasive marketing strategies
meaning_vi: các chiến lược tiếp thị mang tính thuyết phục

examples.en: Firms invest heavily in persuasive marketing strategies to differentiate themselves from competitors.

title: persuasive messages
meaning_vi: thông điệp thuyết phục

examples.en: Bombarded with persuasive messages from rival brands, shoppers often find it difficult to judge which product truly suits their needs.

title: persuasive messaging
meaning_vi: thông điệp mang tính thuyết phục

examples.en: The campaign relied on persuasive messaging to convince customers that the product was indispensable.

title: persuasive tactic
meaning_vi: chiến thuật thuyết phục

examples.en: Creating a false sense of scarcity is a common persuasive tactic used to push customers toward immediate purchases.

title: persuasive techniques
meaning_vi: kỹ thuật thuyết phục

examples.en: Advertisers rely on a range of persuasive techniques, from humour to celebrity endorsement, to capture audience attention.

title: persuasive techniques and emotional appeals
meaning_vi: kỹ thuật thuyết phục và yếu tố kêu gọi cảm xúc

examples.en: The commercial combined persuasive techniques and emotional appeals to convince viewers of the product's value.

title: persuasive techniques used in advertising
meaning_vi: các kỹ thuật thuyết phục được sử dụng trong quảng cáo

examples.en: Marketers are trained to master persuasive techniques used in advertising, such as emotional appeals and scarcity.

title: pervasive slogans and branding
meaning_vi: khẩu hiệu và thương hiệu phổ biến khắp nơi

examples.en: From billboards to bus stops, pervasive slogans and branding ensure that a company's name is rarely out of sight.

title: primary objective
meaning_vi: mục tiêu chính

examples.en: The primary objective of most advertising campaigns is to increase brand awareness rather than to inform consumers of factual product details.

title: product differentiation
meaning_vi: sự khác biệt hóa sản phẩm

examples.en: Effective advertising highlights product differentiation so that customers can compare competing brands.

title: promote it through advertising
meaning_vi: quảng bá sản phẩm thông qua quảng cáo

examples.en: Even a well-designed product still needs a company to promote it through advertising to reach new buyers.

title: reach potential customers
meaning_vi: tiếp cận khách hàng tiềm năng

examples.en: Small businesses can now reach potential customers worldwide through inexpensive online advertising.

title: repeated exposure
meaning_vi: sự tiếp xúc lặp đi lặp lại

examples.en: Repeated exposure to the same advertisement gradually makes a brand name feel familiar and trustworthy, regardless of product quality.

title: sophisticated marketing strategies
meaning_vi: chiến lược tiếp thị tinh vi

examples.en: Retailers now employ sophisticated marketing strategies that track shoppers' behaviour across multiple devices.

title: the local's taste
meaning_vi: khẩu vị, thị hiếu của người dân địa phương

examples.en: International fast-food chains often adjust their menus to suit the local's taste before advertising nationwide.

title: To exemplify
meaning_vi: (phrase (linking)). để minh họa, lấy ví dụ

examples.en: To exemplify, consider how skincare adverts consistently link their products with youthful, glowing skin.

title: boosts profits
meaning_vi: tăng lợi nhuận

examples.en: Effective branding not only attracts new customers but also boosts profits over the long run.

title: drives sales
meaning_vi: thúc đẩy doanh số

examples.en: A well-timed advertising campaign around the holiday season typically drives sales significantly.

title: essential driver of business success
meaning_vi: động lực thiết yếu cho sự thành công của doanh nghiệp

examples.en: Many economists agree that effective branding is an essential driver of business success in competitive markets.

title: local retailers
meaning_vi: nhà bán lẻ địa phương

examples.en: Small local retailers often cannot compete with the vast advertising budgets of multinational corporations.

title: market innovation
meaning_vi: đổi mới thị trường

examples.en: Fierce competition driven by advertising can accelerate market innovation, benefiting consumers with better and cheaper alternatives.

title: penetration
meaning_vi: sự thâm nhập (thị trường)

title: to boost sales
meaning_vi: thúc đẩy doanh số

examples.en: The company launched a limited-time discount campaign to boost sales during the holiday season.

title: boost public interest
meaning_vi: thúc đẩy sự quan tâm của công chúng

examples.en: A well-funded advertising campaign can boost public interest in a sport almost overnight.

title: boost the popularity of sports
meaning_vi: thúc đẩy sự phổ biến của thể thao

examples.en: Global sponsorship deals have done a great deal to boost the popularity of sports like rugby overseas.

title: celebrity endorsements
meaning_vi: sự chứng thực của người nổi tiếng

examples.en: Celebrity endorsements can dramatically boost a brand's credibility among younger audiences.

title: corporate sponsorship
meaning_vi: tài trợ của doanh nghiệp

examples.en: Without corporate sponsorship, many local football clubs would struggle to survive financially.

title: cover training, travel, and event costs
term: cover training, travel, and event costs
meaning_vi: chi trả chi phí huấn luyện, di chuyển và tổ chức sự kiện

examples.en: Sponsorship deals allow athletics federations to cover training, travel, and event costs for young competitors.

title: external backing
meaning_vi: sự hậu thuẫn từ bên ngoài

examples.en: The charity marathon only became a national event after receiving external backing from a major bank.

title: international tournaments
meaning_vi: các giải đấu quốc tế

examples.en: Corporate funding has enabled smaller nations to send their teams to compete in international tournaments.

title: maximize viewership
meaning_vi: tối đa hóa lượng người xem

examples.en: Broadcasters often reschedule matches to unusual times simply to maximize viewership in lucrative overseas markets.

title: media exposure
meaning_vi: sự xuất hiện trên truyền thông

examples.en: Sponsors benefit from significant media exposure whenever their logo appears on a winning athlete's jersey.

title: raise the profile of sports
meaning_vi: nâng cao vị thế của môn thể thao

examples.en: Celebrity endorsements have helped raise the profile of sports that were once largely ignored by the media.

title: Repeated exposure to
meaning_vi: sự tiếp xúc lặp lại với

examples.en: Repeated exposure to glamorous celebrity endorsements can distort young viewers' sense of what an ordinary lifestyle looks like.

title: manufacture demand
meaning_vi: tạo ra nhu cầu giả tạo

examples.en: Some corporations manufacture demand for products that consumers never actually needed in the first place.

title: relentless surge
meaning_vi: làn sóng không ngừng

examples.en: The relentless surge of advertisements across every platform leaves many consumers feeling overwhelmed rather than informed.

title: saturated marketplaces
meaning_vi: thị trường bão hòa

examples.en: In saturated marketplaces, even established brands must innovate constantly to retain their customer base.

title: flop
meaning_vi: thất bại (sản phẩm, chiến dịch)

examples.en: Even with a huge advertising budget, the new soft drink turned out to be a commercial flop.

title: comes at the cost of integrity and values
term: comes at the cost of integrity and values
pronunciation: /kʌmz æt ðə kɒst əv ɪnˈtɛgrɪti ænd ˈvæljuːz/
meaning_vi: phải trả giá bằng sự chính trực và các giá trị

examples.en: Some fans feel that the sport's rapid commercial growth comes at the cost of integrity and values.

title: money-driven decisions
meaning_vi: những quyết định vì lợi ích tiền bạc

examples.en: Some clubs have been accused of making money-driven decisions that ignore the interests of loyal fans.

title: over-commercialization of sports
meaning_vi: sự thương mại hóa quá mức của thể thao

examples.en: Critics argue that the over-commercialization of sports has turned athletes into walking billboards.

title: prioritize marketable players
meaning_vi: ưu tiên những cầu thủ có giá trị thương mại

examples.en: Team managers sometimes prioritize marketable players over more skilful but less photogenic teammates.

title: sportsmanship and fair play
meaning_vi: tinh thần thể thao và sự công bằng

examples.en: Coaches worry that a growing obsession with sponsorship deals is undermining sportsmanship and fair play.

title: genuine storytelling
meaning_vi: kể chuyện chân thực

examples.en: Brands that rely on genuine storytelling rather than exaggerated claims tend to build more lasting trust with consumers.

title: informative campaign
meaning_vi: chiến dịch mang tính cung cấp thông tin

examples.en: The health ministry launched an informative campaign to educate the public about nutrition labels.

title: shift towards innovation and product quality
term: shift towards innovation and product quality
meaning_vi: sự chuyển hướng sang đổi mới và chất lượng sản phẩm

examples.en: Facing stricter regulation, the industry made a clear shift towards innovation and product quality rather than flashy marketing.

title: offering high-quality products
meaning_vi: cung cấp sản phẩm chất lượng cao

examples.en: Even when offering high-quality products, small businesses struggle to reach customers without a substantial advertising presence.

title: stimulating innovation
meaning_vi: kích thích sự đổi mới

examples.en: Advertising can play a positive role in stimulating innovation, as firms are pushed to develop superior products to outshine their rivals' campaigns.

title: a product adequately meets the demands of customers
term: a product adequately meets the demands of customers
pronunciation: /ə ˈprɒdʌkt ˈædɪkwətli miːts ðə dɪˈmɑːndz əv ˈkʌstəməz/
meaning_vi: một sản phẩm đáp ứng đầy đủ nhu cầu của khách hàng

examples.en: When a product adequately meets the demands of customers, word-of-mouth alone can drive strong sales.

title: associate the product with said advantages
term: associate the product with said advantages
meaning_vi: liên tưởng sản phẩm với những lợi ích đã nêu

examples.en: Repeated exposure to the advert makes consumers associate the product with said advantages almost instinctively.

title: discretionary purchases
meaning_vi: các khoản mua sắm không thiết yếu, tùy ý

examples.en: Aggressive advertising often encourages consumers to make discretionary purchases they had not planned.

title: driven by emotional triggers
meaning_vi: bị chi phối bởi các yếu tố kích hoạt cảm xúc

examples.en: Purchases of luxury items are frequently driven by emotional triggers rather than genuine necessity.

title: enhanced self-worth
meaning_vi: giá trị bản thân được nâng cao

examples.en: By suggesting that ownership brings enhanced self-worth, advertisers persuade consumers to equate material possessions with personal success.

title: functional value
meaning_vi: giá trị chức năng (công dụng thực tế)

examples.en: Despite clever marketing, consumers ultimately judge a product by its functional value rather than its image.

title: human's psyche
meaning_vi: tâm lý con người

examples.en: Advertisers study the human's psyche closely to design campaigns that resonate emotionally with viewers.

title: influencing consumers' perceptions
meaning_vi: ảnh hưởng đến nhận thức của người tiêu dùng

examples.en: Advertising is remarkably effective at influencing consumers' perceptions of what counts as a necessity in daily life.

title: intrinsic quality
meaning_vi: chất lượng nội tại

examples.en: Some shoppers judge a product purely on its intrinsic quality, ignoring flashy advertising altogether.

title: long-term customer loyalty
meaning_vi: lòng trung thành của khách hàng lâu dài

examples.en: Consistent product quality is often more effective than discounts at building long-term customer loyalty.

title: non-essential goods
meaning_vi: hàng hóa không thiết yếu

examples.en: Aggressive marketing often persuades households to spend beyond their means on non-essential goods that offer little long-term value.

title: nonessential good
meaning_vi: hàng hóa không thiết yếu

examples.en: Advertisers frequently rebrand a nonessential good as a must-have item to drive impulse buying.

title: peer influence
meaning_vi: ảnh hưởng từ bạn bè đồng trang lứa

examples.en: Teenagers are particularly susceptible to peer influence when deciding which brands to wear.

title: products that are congruent with their needs
term: products that are congruent with their needs
pronunciation: /ˈprɒdʌkts ðət ə ˈkɒŋgruənt wɪð ðeə niːdz/

examples.en: Consumers tend to remain loyal to brands that consistently offer products that are congruent with their needs.

title: purchasing decisions
meaning_vi: quyết định mua hàng

examples.en: Advertisements shape purchasing decisions by associating products with desirable lifestyles rather than practical benefits.

title: recommend it to their friends and colleagues
term: recommend it to their friends and colleagues
pronunciation: /ˌrekəˈmend ɪt tə ðeə frendz ən ˈkɒliːgz/

examples.en: Once customers trust a brand, they are far more likely to recommend it to their friends and colleagues.

title: shift people's perception
meaning_vi: làm thay đổi nhận thức của con người

examples.en: Sustainability campaigns have started to shift people's perception of what a responsible brand looks like.

title: shopping preferences
meaning_vi: sở thích mua sắm

examples.en: The idea that advertising has no effect on shopping preferences has gained traction among some economists.

title: social proof
meaning_vi: bằng chứng xã hội

examples.en: Displaying thousands of five-star reviews gives an online store powerful social proof that boosts sales.

title: to memorize the product's benefits subconsciously
term: to memorize the product's benefits subconsciously
meaning_vi: ghi nhớ lợi ích của sản phẩm một cách vô thức

examples.en: Catchy jingles help viewers to memorize the product's benefits subconsciously long after the advert ends.

title: usage pattern
meaning_vi: mô hình sử dụng, thói quen sử dụng

examples.en: Companies analyze customers' usage pattern to tailor advertisements to their specific needs.

title: word of mouth
meaning_vi: truyền miệng

examples.en: Most of the café's new customers arrived through word of mouth rather than any formal advertising.

title: word-of-mouth credibility
meaning_vi: độ tin cậy truyền miệng

examples.en: A single glowing recommendation from a friend often carries more word-of-mouth credibility than a paid advert.

title: adversely impact their purchasing habits
meaning_vi: tác động tiêu cực đến thói quen mua sắm của họ

examples.en: Constant exposure to luxury advertising can adversely impact their purchasing habits and lead to overspending.

title: artificial desire
meaning_vi: nhu cầu giả tạo

examples.en: Critics argue that advertisements manufacture an artificial desire for products that consumers would otherwise never consider purchasing.

title: cognitive overload
meaning_vi: quá tải nhận thức

examples.en: Researchers warn that excessive advertising contributes to cognitive overload, making it harder for people to focus on genuine needs.

title: constant pressure to consume
meaning_vi: áp lực tiêu dùng liên tục

examples.en: Social media influencers subject their followers to constant pressure to consume the latest products.

title: constant upgrading
meaning_vi: việc nâng cấp liên tục

examples.en: Technology advertisements encourage constant upgrading of devices, fuelling a culture of waste and unnecessary consumption.

title: decision fatigue
meaning_vi: sự mệt mỏi khi ra quyết định

examples.en: Constant advertising for near-identical products can cause decision fatigue, leaving consumers unable to choose confidently.

title: dissatisfaction and a sense of inadequacy
term: dissatisfaction and a sense of inadequacy
meaning_vi: sự bất mãn và cảm giác không đủ tốt

examples.en: Constant exposure to glamorous ads can breed dissatisfaction and a sense of inadequacy in viewers.

title: dissatisfied with
meaning_vi: không hài lòng với

examples.en: Frequent advertising for the latest gadgets can leave consumers permanently dissatisfied with what they already own.

title: encourage impulsive buying
meaning_vi: khuyến khích mua sắm bốc đồng

examples.en: Flash sales and countdown timers on websites encourage impulsive buying among online shoppers.

title: exploit psychological triggers
meaning_vi: khai thác các yếu tố kích hoạt tâm lý

examples.en: Some marketers exploit psychological triggers such as fear of missing out to pressure shoppers into hasty purchases.

title: feel discontented
meaning_vi: cảm thấy bất mãn, không hài lòng

examples.en: Consumers who constantly compare themselves to advertised lifestyles often feel discontented with their own lives.

title: feel inadequate or dissatisfied
meaning_vi: cảm thấy thiếu thốn hoặc không hài lòng

title: fosters impulsive spending habits
meaning_vi: thúc đẩy thói quen chi tiêu bốc đồng

examples.en: Constant notification alerts from shopping apps fosters impulsive spending habits among users.

title: impulse buying
meaning_vi: mua sắm bốc đồng

examples.en: Limited-time offers are specifically designed to encourage impulse buying rather than considered purchasing decisions.

title: impulse purchase
meaning_vi: mua sắm bốc đồng, không có kế hoạch

examples.en: Bright checkout displays are designed specifically to trigger an impulse purchase.

title: impulsive spending
meaning_vi: chi tiêu bốc đồng

examples.en: Flash sales advertised on social media often trigger impulsive spending that shoppers later regret.

title: sense of inadequacy
meaning_vi: cảm giác thiếu thốn, không đủ tốt

examples.en: Viewing heavily edited photos on social media can trigger a deep sense of inadequacy among young users.

title: sway individuals into making purchases
meaning_vi: tác động khiến cá nhân thực hiện mua sắm

title: swayed by advertisements
meaning_vi: bị tác động, lung lay bởi quảng cáo

title: yearnings

title: tighter household budgets
meaning_vi: ngân sách gia đình eo hẹp hơn

title: cognizant of
meaning_vi: nhận thức được về

title: consumer awareness
meaning_vi: nhận thức của người tiêu dùng

title: consumer scepticism
meaning_vi: sự hoài nghi của người tiêu dùng

title: educate and guide first-time consumers

title: educate first-time buyers
meaning_vi: giáo dục người mua lần đầu

title: help a customer make their final decision

title: informed decision-making

title: make informed choices
meaning_vi: đưa ra lựa chọn sáng suốt, có đầy đủ thông tin

title: make informed purchasing decisions
meaning_vi: đưa ra quyết định mua hàng sáng suốt

examples.en: Detailed product reviews help customers make informed purchasing decisions before spending their money.

title: make well-informed decisions

examples.en: Educational campaigns encourage more mindful consumer behavior by highlighting the environmental cost of overconsumption.

meaning_vi: hành vi tìm kiếm dựa trên nhu cầu

title: prioritize essential spending
meaning_vi: ưu tiên các khoản chi tiêu thiết yếu

title: research‐driven decision making
meaning_vi: việc ra quyết định dựa trên nghiên cứu

examples.en: As access to online reviews grows, research-driven decision making is gradually replacing reliance on advertising alone.

title: responsible consumption pattern
meaning_vi: mô hình tiêu dùng có trách nhiệm

title: responsible purchasing habits
meaning_vi: thói quen mua sắm có trách nhiệm

examples.en: Financial education can help young people develop responsible purchasing habits despite the constant pressure of advertising.

meaning_vi: con dao hai lưỡi

examples.en: Social media advertising is a double-edged sword, offering wide reach but also risking privacy violations.

title: paid impression
meaning_vi: lượt hiển thị trả phí

meaning_vi: nội dung quảng cáo

meaning_vi: thiết kế quảng cáo riêng cho từng cá nhân

meaning_vi: quảng cáo mạng xã hội có mục tiêu

title: the advent of targeted advertising
meaning_vi: sự xuất hiện của quảng cáo nhắm mục tiêu

title: the masses

meaning_vi: chi phối quyết định của người tiêu dùng

meaning_vi: phần mềm chặn quảng cáo

title: ad‐suppression technologies
meaning_vi: công nghệ chặn quảng cáo

meaning_vi: không bị gián đoạn bởi quảng cáo thương mại

title: price‐comparison platform
meaning_vi: nền tảng so sánh giá

title: subscribing to ad-free services
meaning_vi: đăng ký các dịch vụ không quảng cáo

examples.en: Many streaming platform users are subscribing to ad-free services despite the extra monthly cost.

title: using ad-blocking software
meaning_vi: sử dụng phần mềm chặn quảng cáo

examples.en: Frustrated by intrusive pop-ups, an increasing number of internet users are now using ad-blocking software.

title: claims made in advertisements
meaning_vi: những tuyên bố trong quảng cáo

meaning_vi: thông điệp quảng cáo mâu thuẫn

term: create a false sense of necessity
meaning_vi: tạo ra cảm giác cần thiết giả tạo

meaning_vi: tuyên bố lừa dối

title: employ manipulative tactics
meaning_vi: sử dụng thủ đoạn thao túng

meaning_vi: những ưu đãi khuyến mãi bị phóng đại

meaning_vi: xâm phạm quyền riêng tư

title: marketing exaggerations
meaning_vi: sự phóng đại trong tiếp thị

meaning_vi: lợi dụng sự bất an hoặc tạo ra nhu cầu giả tạo

title: sends mixed messages
meaning_vi: gửi đi những thông điệp mâu thuẫn

title: the erosion of privacy
meaning_vi: sự xói mòn quyền riêng tư

title: the intrusive nature of advertising
meaning_vi: bản chất xâm phạm của quảng cáo

meaning_vi: các ngành công nghiệp không lành mạnh hoặc gây tranh cãi

term: a blanket ban on all forms of advertising

title: become more discerning consumers
meaning_vi: trở thành người tiêu dùng sáng suốt hơn

examples.en: With better education, people can become more discerning consumers who are harder to mislead.

title: critically evaluate advertising messages
meaning_vi: đánh giá phê phán các thông điệp quảng cáo

examples.en: Schools should teach students to critically evaluate advertising messages so that they are less easily manipulated as adults.

title: frequency caps
meaning_vi: giới hạn tần suất

examples.en: Introducing frequency caps on television commercials would reduce the sense of being bombarded with the same advertisement repeatedly.

title: improve product quality and transparency
meaning_vi: cải thiện chất lượng sản phẩm và tính minh bạch

examples.en: Stricter advertising regulations would compel companies to improve product quality and transparency rather than rely on flashy campaigns.

title: media literacy
meaning_vi: hiểu biết về truyền thông

examples.en: Improving media literacy in schools would equip children with the skills to question rather than blindly trust advertisements.

title: preventive measure
meaning_vi: biện pháp phòng ngừa

examples.en: Regulators introduced stricter disclosure rules as a preventive measure against misleading advertising.

title: promote media literacy
meaning_vi: thúc đẩy hiểu biết về truyền thông

examples.en: Schools should promote media literacy so that students can recognise manipulative advertising techniques.

title: raised public consciousness
meaning_vi: nâng cao nhận thức của công chúng

examples.en: Government-funded campaigns have raised public consciousness about deceptive advertising tactics.

title: truth-in-advertising statutes
meaning_vi: luật quảng cáo trung thực

examples.en: Strong truth-in-advertising statutes are essential to prevent companies from misleading vulnerable consumers.

title: uphold higher standards of quality and accountability
term: uphold higher standards of quality and accountability

examples.en: Independent advertising watchdogs push businesses to uphold higher standards of quality and accountability in their promotional claims.

title: consumer-driven society
meaning_vi: xã hội tiêu dùng, xã hội bị chi phối bởi tiêu dùng

title: omnipresent force
meaning_vi: thế lực hiện diện khắp nơi

title: the increasing ubiquity of advertising
meaning_vi: sự hiện diện khắp nơi ngày càng tăng của quảng cáo

examples.en: The increasing ubiquity of advertising means consumers now encounter brand messages almost everywhere they go.

title: the pervasive nature of advertising
meaning_vi: bản chất lan tỏa khắp nơi của quảng cáo

examples.en: The pervasive nature of advertising means that consumers encounter marketing messages almost everywhere they go.

title: the prevalence of advertising
meaning_vi: sự phổ biến của quảng cáo

examples.en: The prevalence of advertising in everyday life makes it almost impossible to avoid commercial messages.

title: wields immense influence over
meaning_vi: nắm giữ ảnh hưởng to lớn đối với

title: generates significant tax revenue
meaning_vi: tạo ra nguồn thu thuế đáng kể

term: serves as a catalyst for businesses to thrive

meaning_vi: đóng vai trò chất xúc tác giúp doanh nghiệp phát triển

examples.en: Well-targeted advertising serves as a catalyst for businesses to thrive in crowded markets.

title: stimulates economic growth
meaning_vi: kích thích tăng trưởng kinh tế

examples.en: Economists argue that a competitive advertising sector stimulates economic growth by encouraging innovation.

title: supports job creation
meaning_vi: hỗ trợ tạo việc làm

examples.en: The advertising industry supports job creation not only for marketers but also for designers and content creators.

title: trillions of dollars being poured in advertising
term: trillions of dollars being poured in advertising
pronunciation: /ˈtrɪljənz əv ˈdɒləz ˈbiːɪŋ pɔːd ɪn ˈædvətaɪzɪŋ/
meaning_vi: hàng nghìn tỷ đô la được đổ vào quảng cáo

examples.en: With trillions of dollars being poured in advertising yearly around the world, its economic influence is undeniable.

title: a profound effect
meaning_vi: một tác động sâu sắc

examples.en: Repeated exposure to advertising can have a profound effect on how people define happiness.

title: advertising glut
meaning_vi: sự dư thừa quảng cáo

examples.en: The current advertising glut on streaming platforms has led many viewers to pay for premium, ad-free subscriptions instead.

title: bombarded with
meaning_vi: bị dồn dập tấn công bởi

title: boosting consumerism culture
meaning_vi: thúc đẩy văn hóa tiêu dùng

examples.en: Critics claim that relentless advertising is boosting consumerism culture at the expense of the environment.

title: cares less about the wellbeing of the poor
term: cares less about the wellbeing of the poor
pronunciation: /keəz les əˈbaʊt ðə ˈwelbiːɪŋ əv ðə pʊə/
meaning_vi: ít quan tâm đến phúc lợi của người nghèo

examples.en: Opponents claim that the advertising industry cares less about the wellbeing of the poor than about profit margins.

title: constant bombardment of such ads
meaning_vi: sự dồn dập liên tục của những quảng cáo như vậy

examples.en: Many users complain that the constant bombardment of such ads makes browsing the internet exhausting.

title: contributing to a materialistic mindset
meaning_vi: góp phần hình thành tư duy vật chất

examples.en: Critics claim that relentless advertising is contributing to a materialistic mindset among young people.

title: create an aspirational culture
meaning_vi: tạo ra một nền văn hóa khát vọng, đua đòi

examples.en: Luxury advertising helps create an aspirational culture in which status symbols define personal success.

title: creates a materialist society
meaning_vi: tạo ra một xã hội trọng vật chất

examples.en: Some sociologists argue that relentless advertising creates a materialist society obsessed with possessions.

title: creates more waste
meaning_vi: tạo ra nhiều rác thải hơn

examples.en: Encouraging constant upgrades through advertising creates more waste in an already overburdened environment.

title: depreciation
meaning_vi: sự sụt giảm giá trị

examples.en: Some experts argue that overexposure to advertising causes a depreciation of genuine cultural values.

title: eroding the quality of life
meaning_vi: làm suy giảm chất lượng cuộc sống

examples.en: Critics argue that constant commercial noise is slowly eroding the quality of life in modern cities.

title: exposed to a ceaseless stream of advertisements
term: exposed to a ceaseless stream of advertisements

examples.en: Commuters are exposed to a ceaseless stream of advertisements on billboards, buses, and mobile apps.

title: financial strain and disillusionment
meaning_vi: áp lực tài chính và sự vỡ mộng

examples.en: Chasing trends advertised online often leaves consumers with financial strain and disillusionment.

title: idealized image of success portrayed in ads
term: idealized image of success portrayed in ads

meaning_vi: hình ảnh lý tưởng hóa về thành công được khắc họa trong quảng cáo

examples.en: The idealized image of success portrayed in ads rarely reflects the everyday realities of ordinary consumers.

title: imprinting them in the collective consciousness
term: imprinting them in the collective consciousness
meaning_vi: khắc sâu chúng vào ý thức tập thể

examples.en: Iconic jingles succeed by imprinting them in the collective consciousness of an entire generation.

title: information overload
meaning_vi: quá tải thông tin

examples.en: The constant stream of advertisements contributes to information overload, making it harder for people to identify what is truly relevant.

title: mass production and disposal
meaning_vi: sản xuất và thải bỏ hàng loạt

examples.en: Fast fashion advertising fuels a cycle of mass production and disposal that harms the planet.

title: perpetuate unrealistic standards and ideals
meaning_vi: duy trì những chuẩn mực và lý tưởng phi thực tế

examples.en: Critics argue that beauty advertisements perpetuate unrealistic standards and ideals that damage self-image.

title: promote an unrealistic standard of success
term: promote an unrealistic standard of success
meaning_vi: quảng bá một chuẩn mực thành công phi thực tế

examples.en: Luxury brands often promote an unrealistic standard of success that few consumers can ever attain.

title: social costs
meaning_vi: chi phí xã hội

examples.en: Policymakers are beginning to weigh the social costs of advertising against its clear economic advantages.

title: takes a heavy toll on
meaning_vi: gây tổn hại nặng nề đến

examples.en: Excessive exposure to idealized advertisements takes a heavy toll on teenagers' self-esteem.

title: the overabundance of advertisements
meaning_vi: sự dư thừa quảng cáo

examples.en: The overabundance of advertisements on streaming platforms has led many users to pay for ad-free subscriptions.

title: be detrimental to the economy
meaning_vi: gây tổn hại đến nền kinh tế

examples.en: A sudden collapse of the advertising industry would be detrimental to the economy as a whole.

title: effects of economic downturns
meaning_vi: những tác động của suy thoái kinh tế

examples.en: Advertising budgets are usually the first to be cut during the effects of economic downturns.

title: increased consumer spending
meaning_vi: chi tiêu tiêu dùng gia tăng

examples.en: Successful marketing campaigns are often linked to periods of increased consumer spending nationwide.

title: stifle economic progress
meaning_vi: kìm hãm sự phát triển kinh tế

examples.en: Banning advertising outright could stifle economic progress by depriving businesses of a vital sales channel.

title: decreased consumerism
meaning_vi: chủ nghĩa tiêu dùng suy giảm

examples.en: Some sociologists argue that decreased consumerism would ultimately benefit both the environment and mental health.

title: reduces the environmental footprint
meaning_vi: giảm dấu chân môi trường

examples.en: Buying fewer, higher-quality goods reduces the environmental footprint of everyday consumption.

title: social-impact initiative
meaning_vi: sáng kiến tác động xã hội

examples.en: The company launched a social-impact initiative to fund scholarships for underprivileged students.

title: promoting healthy competition and fostering innovation
term: promoting healthy competition and fostering innovation
meaning_vi: thúc đẩy cạnh tranh lành mạnh và khuyến khích đổi mới

examples.en: By promoting healthy competition and fostering innovation, advertising ultimately benefits consumers through lower prices.

title: detrimental
meaning_vi: có hại

examples.en: Excessive advertising aimed at children can be detrimental to their perception of body image.

title: age-appropriate content
meaning_vi: nội dung phù hợp với lứa tuổi

examples.en: Regulators should require broadcasters to guarantee age-appropriate content when advertisements are shown during children's programmes.
